summary: The single blocking thermal-controller lifecycle defect B1 is resolved and its original running/paused timeout failures now pass focused CPU-mock rechecks. No remaining source blockers were found. M1 architecture, training, frozen evaluation and GT-path findings from the initial review remain applicable because the other seven new sources are unchanged. Source acceptance only: no neural/CUDA runtime validation or hardware-limit approval.
reviewer_context: fresh native Codex subagent /root/review_common_outlet_m1_thermal; runtime model identity is not independently exposed in this reviewer context

correct_as_inspected.topic: Single M1 factor and active query
correct_as_inspected.evidence: CommonOutletAxis wraps the inherited common head with one trainable 512D query residual for every pooling; CommonOutletDeMo applies the same wrapper. Mean controls therefore use the query in their common descriptor rather than carrying idle parameter padding. Query construction uses a separate CPU Generator and adds no global sampling RNG draw. original_mean delegates fuse to the unchanged V12 class.

eligible_mean averages the same projected, anchored, route-mass-weighted M/I rows over eligible relations. seed_query uses a single normalized query against actual routed M keys, with sqrt(512) scaling and invalid-relation masking, then aggregates those same M/I rows. It is not a 21-token PMA. Frequency keeps its existing independent increment. Nonempty retained sets imply eligible counts 1, 3 or 7, so the denominator is nonzero on the actual protocol.

correct_as_inspected.topic: Private coordinates, metric mass and controlled states
correct_as_inspected.evidence: The new fuse preserves base[:, :5120] and changes only the common block before the inherited sqrt(.75)/sqrt(.25) normalization. Masks still come from valid source subsets. Controlled state10 uses independent m0 and its own relation scores; state01 uses independent f0. last_outlet_weights is diagnostic only and is not read as state input. No new state leakage was found.

The wrapper reuses run_shared_identity_experiment, configuration, losses, full/partial update, sampler and scheduler. It persists args.pooling before run.json/result.json construction. Fifty epochs, B64, K4, seed42, native GradScaler512, earliest dev-mAP tie and fresh publicCLIP remain wired. The per-epoch and per-batch partial-set generator code is unchanged.

The verifier is wired for nine augmented initial state comparisons plus the DeMo shared-head comparison and all ten by seven availability checks. It includes private zero masks, common squared mass .25, seeded original_mean parity against CommonCoordinateAxis, isolated query RNG, and stopped gallery checks. All ten three-update native smokes check every trainable parameter for finite nonzero gradient and strict in-memory reload. Both smoke queues finish successfully before any train command is submitted. These checks have not run on a model during this review.

correct_as_inspected.topic: Frozen evaluation and independent GT paths
correct_as_inspected.evidence: Both frozen wrappers reconstruct arguments including pooling and strict-load the specified best.pth. Each run has 49 frozen availability pairs and 294 six-state cases. Normal features and previous full11 metrics/per-query CSVs must match. The CPU wrapper points each explicitly named pooling/variant run to pooling/controlled_states/MSVR310_<variant>_s42/full. The inherited auditor reconstructs IDs/cameras/scenes from installed MSVR training filenames and fixed dev IDs, excludes same-ID/same-scene entries, lexicographically ranks stored FP32 distances, and recounts six metrics, CMC50, groups, per-query values and contribution arithmetic.

correct_as_inspected.topic: Normal thermal path and resource scope
correct_as_inspected.evidence: The current normal path rejects 350W before Popen, rejects physical GPU0/1, sets CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES to the selected physical GPU2/3, creates a new process group, pauses at >=75C or power draw/limit >250W and resumes the same group only at <=70C and <=250W. Local monitoring sleeps 5 seconds; capacity waiting is 240 seconds. Existing four CPU mocks pass. This does not validate physical thermal response.

The revised finally owns cleanup immediately after successful Popen; running and paused timeout cases both terminate only the owned group, reap it and write a failure receipt before propagating the original exception. The separate mocked replays verified exact exception-object preservation and one wait per child.

original_failure_case_replays.harness: In-memory stdlib mock replay against the final unmodified guard. Popen/getpgid/killpg/time.sleep/telemetry patched. Reused the original fake owned PGID4242 and initial cap250W/temp60C/draw200W/memory0MiB. TemporaryDirectory outputs only.

deployment_gates.evidence: results/preflight/gpu_thermal_power_policy_20261003.json records both selected GPUs still capped at 350W at 2026-10-03T22:50:20, with direct and sudo-n administrative setting attempts rejected. This reviewer did not re-query the host.
deployment_gates.requirement: Do not launch a neural task until actual physical GPU2/3 power limits are observed <=250W. A source fix does not satisfy this hardware prerequisite.

After source remediation/review and the hardware prerequisite, the actual tensor verifier and all ten smokes must pass before training. Expected parameter counts and source consistency are not model validation.

After controller completion, run the existing audit_common_outlet_states.py with the campaign root, installed data root and fixed splits. The launcher does not invoke that separate CPU audit; its controller COMPLETE alone is not independent-GT acceptance.

limitations: No SSH, deployment, administrator action, real nvidia-smi query, CUDA process, model import/construction/forward/backward or training was performed.
All thermal executions were CPU mocks. Real Linux signal delivery, actual power limiting, temperature overshoot/cooldown and uninterrupted optimizer/sampler state during suspension remain unverified.
No local Torch or NumPy is installed in the selected interpreter. No actual installed-dataset GT recount or checkpoint evaluation was performed.
Source inspection supports the formulas and dataflow but does not establish numerical CUDA parity, measured parameter counts, utility or completion of any of the ten experiments.
This fresh context is same-family review only and has provisional acceptance status; no cross-family independence is claimed.

blockers.title: Thermal-monitor failure abandons the owned child process group
blockers.finding: Popen creates a separate session and the monitoring loop may SIGSTOP its process group. telemetry uses a real subprocess.check_output timeout of 15 seconds. There is no post-Popen try/finally cleanup. If telemetry raises, execute propagates the exception while the child remains alive; an already stopped child stays stopped indefinitely. No child.wait or failure exit receipt is reached. A running child instead continues without the thermal supervisor.
blockers.evidence: Two deterministic mock reproductions executed against the current unmodified gpu_thermal_execute module, with fake owned PID/PGID 4242 and no real subprocess or GPU query. Details are retained in tests_actually_run.failure_reproduction.
blockers.minimal_fix: Wrap the lifetime after successful Popen in a finally that, when the child is still alive, sends SIGKILL only to that newly created owned process group and reaps it with wait. SIGKILL also handles an already SIGSTOP-ed group without temporarily resuming unmonitored computation. Preserve an explicit failure receipt and propagate the original error. No retry, fallback, restart or peer-GPU action is needed.
blockers.required_recheck: Re-run the existing four mocks and both timeout cases. The running and paused timeout cases must end with own-group cleanup and wait, retain the error, and leave no live child.

failure_reproduction.harness: In-memory stdlib unittest.mock test imported gpu_thermal_execute, patched Popen/getpgid/killpg/time.sleep and supplied telemetry samples followed by subprocess.TimeoutExpired("nvidia-smi", 15). Output files were confined to TemporaryDirectory and removed on context exit.

harness_preparation_failures: Bare PATH python failed before testing with "No pyvenv.cfg file". Used the already installed uv-managed CPython; no environment or package was installed.

First in-memory source-check harness omitted encoding and hit Windows GBK UnicodeDecodeError reading the UTF-8 plan. Corrected the harness to read UTF-8 and reran successfully; no project source was changed.

resolved_blockers.title: Thermal-monitor failure abandons the owned child process group
resolved_blockers.resolution: A finally now covers the successfully spawned child lifetime. If child.poll reports the child is still alive, cleanup sends SIGKILL only to child.pid as its owned process group; it then calls wait and writes exit_code and forced_own_group_cleanup. The pending sensor exception propagates after the finally. A normally exited child is reaped without a kill. No retry, fallback, restart or peer-GPU action was added.
resolved_blockers.validation: All six updated CPU mocks pass. Both original failure scenarios were separately replayed with the same fake owned PGID4242; running timeout produced SIGKILL then wait, paused timeout produced SIGSTOP then SIGKILL then wait. Both wrote exit_code=-9 / forced_own_group_cleanup=true and preserved the exact original TimeoutExpired object. One Popen call per case, no real child or GPU query.
resolved_blockers.original_failure_evidence: Retained verbatim under initial_review_evidence.tests_actually_run.failure_reproduction and in the byte-exact archived first review.
